answer: On a terrace growing yarrow, maintenance agents earn credits for keeping irrigation alive. A meter with a hardware-bound identity signs each pump's hourly pulse, and the registry accepts only one earning lease per meter per epoch. Random inspections compare the pulse with water delivered. Making extra agent accounts then requires extra pumps and meters, plus electricity and a bond lost for false readings. Stolen meter keys or colluding inspectors can still forge work, so devices need revocation and independent spot checks.
